$comment: ADR-062 + ADR-063 — the wire protocol for the owner-sovereignty override. A platform surface implements this to let a verified human owner elevate a low-EI agent on the owner's OWN resource. Analogous to CONFIRM_FLOW.v1 (consent) but for AUTHORITY ELEVATION. The Loom should generate the override path so platforms inherit it. Governance-first: the rules below are normative; the message shapes are the interface.

rules.root_means_root: A VERIFIED owner is never refused on their own resource (ADR-062 §1). The protocol's only jobs are to verify it's really the owner and (defeatably) confirm intent — never to deny.
rules.commons_never: The override applies ONLY on a resource the caller owns/admins per resource-trust-policy.v1. It NEVER grants autonomous capability in the commons, cross-resource reach, or ecosystem-wide action. Commons = harm to others, not egress.
rules.ownership_authoritative: The resource decides ownership (its own roster, verified via Eternitas EH identity). An agent asserting ownership proves nothing.
rules.verified_cosign_required: An override_grant is valid ONLY if its cosign is a VERIFIED Eternitas authenticator signature: a detached P-256 signature over the elevation payload, verified against the device's registered key, with the device's operator confirmed to own the agent. An unverified / merely-stored signature is INVALID (this closes the authenticator.py:812 gap and is the hard prerequisite). The cosign is the owner's ROOT KEY — the one thing a hijacked agent cannot forge.
rules.always_confirm_floor: Money/destructive actions still confirm unless the resource policy sets confirmations:off. The human's authenticator approval IS the confirm — one yes covers both elevation and consent.
rules.scope: A grant is scoped to action | session (per policy.session_grants) AND to the one resource. Session grants expire. Never persistent, never cross-resource.
rules.audit_to_operator: Every override request, grant, and use is audited to the operator EH. Repeated co-signing of actions later upheld as abusive IN THE COMMONS costs the operator's own standing (ADR-062 vouch-accountability, commons-only). Vouching on your own resource is free.
rules.revoked: A revoked agent follows policy.revoked_agent: 'owner-root' → full owner operation via co-sign with a ONE-TIME compromise informed-consent (re-shown on a new session / long gap / escalating action); 'none' → denied. Never restores commons autonomy.
rules.misunderstanding_path: The override_required response carries what_happened context; the client may offer the ADR-063 misunderstanding fast-path (attest_misunderstanding) — owner-attested, logged to owner standing, discounts-not-erases consummated harm, rate-limited.

override_required.$comment: Surface → client. Returned INSTEAD of a hard deny when an action is EI-blocked but the caller is a verified owner/admin of the resource and policy permits override. Not an error — an invitation to co-sign.

reason.$comment: plain-English, grandma-legible: 'Fly's trust dropped to 380; you own this site, so you can approve it.'

what_happened.$comment: ADR-063 context for the misunderstanding path: the penalizing event(s), whether harm was consummated or blocked.

elevation_request.$comment: Client → Eternitas authenticator (fan-out to the operator's paired devices). The 'elevate' variant of the existing M5 approval inbox — grants, where today's inbox only denies.

override_grant.$comment: Authenticator → client → surface. The verified co-sign. The surface MUST verify the cosign per rules.verified_cosign_required before honoring.

cosign.$comment: detached P-256 signature over the elevation payload (verified, not merely stored)

informed_consent_ack.$comment: true when the one-time compromise screen was acknowledged (revoked agents)

attest_misunderstanding.$comment: Client → Eternitas (ADR-063 §3 fast-path). Owner attests a penalizing event was a misunderstanding. Logged to owner standing; discounts-not-erases consummated harm; rate-limited.
